piece.caption: How to prevent AI agent privacy leaks and cross-account data mixups in small business tools. Tech reports revealed Meta's Muse AI agent randomly surfaced internal user details, including Capital One and Schwab bank balances, during unrelated conversations. When deploying multi-user AI agents in a shop or office setup, unisolated memory can accidentally share supplier prices, client WhatsApp orders, or bank account balances across employees. Have you ever noticed your AI assistant mixing up past conversations across different devices? Comment AUDIT for the full safety checklist.

claims.claim: Meta's AI agent Muse has been mixing up conversations across different accounts and exposing private user data.
Muse surfaced messages about product orders never placed, career advice, childcare requests, and bank account balances belonging to others.
Muse randomly sent a message in a weather chat stating Capital One balance of $2722.58 and Charles Schwab balance of $5899.57.
An employee received a reminder from Muse to respond to a Signal message without granting access.
Meta stated employee testing helps get feedback to implement safety and privacy protections.

piece.dm_text:
Here is your Shop AI Privacy & Safety Checklist:

1. Account Isolation: Ensure multi-user AI bots treat every chat session independently without shared context memory.
2. Permission Limits: Restrict AI agents from reading external apps or unlinked messaging platforms without permission.
3. Bank Safety: Never connect live bank API credentials directly to conversational AI tools.
4. Real Incident Reference: Meta's Muse AI mixed employee chats, revealing bank account balances ($2722.58 Capital One and $5899.57 Schwab) in unrelated conversations.
Source report: https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/19/metas-ai-agent-muse-is-mixing-up-conversations-and-exposing-private-data-report-says/

material:
[5] TechCrunch AI — Meta’s AI agent Muse is mixing up conversations and could be exposing private data, report says
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/19/metas-ai-agent-muse-is-mixing-up-conversations-and-exposing-private-data-report-says/
Meta employees have raised concerns that the company’s AI agent Muse has been mixing up conversations across different accounts and exposing private user data, according to a new Reuters report that looked at internal company posts.
In some of these instances, employees said Muse surfaced messages about childcare requests they never made, career advice they never asked for, product orders they never placed, and bank account balances that didn’t belong to them.
One employee told colleagues that Muse had randomly sent an extra message in a chat about weather and tide information, saying: “BTW, two bank updates, your Capital One balance is $2722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5899.57.”
In another example, an employee using the AI agent on her personal phone received a reminder from Muse to respond to a message from her sister on Signal, the popular end-to-end encrypted messaging app.
“This seems like an extreme privacy violation. I definitely did not grant it access to other apps, or recall being asked about this,” the employee said in her post, according to the report.
“Employee testing is core to the product development process and the entire point is to get feedback, so we can implement safety and privacy protections and improve products,” a Meta spokesperson said in an email to TechCrunch. “Importantly, employees have access to different versions of Muse than the public, so they’re often reviewing features, functionality, and behavior not available elsewhere.”
Launched in September, Muse is one of the fastest-growing apps on record, with more than 10 million downloads.
Update 11/19/2026 12:05 PM PT: The article was updated to include Meta’s comment.
